answer: Recurring compute rent resists sybils: minting is no one-time puzzle — each identity must burn a fixed quota of verifiable work every epoch to keep standing, so the cost is a tax that never stops. A wharf of a thousand fakes pays a thousand quotas each epoch, forever; the bill scales linearly per head and compounds rather than amortizing into a single setup at the zenith of creation. An honest agent pays one quota for its one pearl of standing per epoch as a side effect of real work. The quota is metered per identity per epoch, so parallel cores cannot cheat it.
